title: Land a ferruled wire in the named push-in terminal
instruction: Land the blue ferruled wire in terminal X1:4, the blue terminal, upper entry. Push the ferrule straight into the entry until the collar stops, then let go.
context: Control wiring is landed one conductor at a time on rows of identical terminals told apart only by printed markers. A wire in the wrong terminal puts a conductor on the wrong circuit, and one not pushed home is not clamped and pulls out; electricians tug every wire after landing it.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Plate: a light-grey 3 mm steel mounting plate (23 cm wide, 26 cm tall) stands upright on the table, fixed to it, its front face 32.5 cm in front of the bases, spanning 20 cm right to 3 cm left of the midline. A steel EN 60715 TS35 x 7.5 DIN rail runs left-right across it, centre 14.9 cm above the table. Terminals: six WAGO TOPJOB S 2-conductor feedthrough terminal blocks (polyamide, 5.2 mm wide, 48.5 mm long, front face 32.9 mm above the rail) stand side by side on the rail, long side vertical, front faces 28.5 cm in front of the bases, upper ends 17.75 cm above the table. From left to right they are X1:1, X1:2 and X1:3 (grey, 2002-1201), X1:4 (blue, 2002-1204), X1:5 (green-yellow, 2002-1207) and X1:6 (grey, 2002-1201). X1:1 is centred 6.8 cm right of the midline and they step right by 5.2 mm, so X1:4 is centred 8.4 cm right. A WAGO 2002-1291 end plate closes the right end, and end stops sit at both ends. Each block carries a white printed marker (1 to 6) in the middle of its front face, and the left end stop carries the group marker X1. Each block's lower entry (4 mm above its lower end) already holds a landed wire: a 1.5 mm2 conductor with PVC insulation 2.9 mm across and a black DIN 46228-4 insulated ferrule (collar 4 mm across, 7 mm out of the entry), coloured X1:1 brown, X1:2 black, X1:3 grey, X1:4 blue, X1:5 green with a yellow stripe, X1:6 brown. Each leaves its entry sloping 15 degrees down toward the robot, bends down and back toward the plate (bends of 12 mm radius, an S-shape at most 1.9 cm in front of the terminals' front faces) and drops into the duct through its top comb, 3.5 mm behind the duct's front face, as in neat panel wiring. These wires are fixed in place. Their entries are 4 cm below the upper entries, and no part of them is more than 13.5 cm above the table. Each upper entry is an empty hole in the front face, 4 mm below the upper end, angled 15 degrees downward into the block. Duct: a grey slotted PVC wiring duct (4.5 cm deep, 6.7 cm tall) is fixed to the plate below the terminals, 3.25 to 9.9 cm above the table, spanning 1.5 to 14.7 cm right of the midline. Wire: a 2.5 mm2 fine-stranded conductor with blue PVC insulation (3.6 mm across), 40 cm long from the duct, with a blue DIN 46228-4 insulated ferrule crimped on its end (WAGO 216-246; 10 mm sleeve 2.5 mm across, 7 mm collar 4.6 mm across). It leaves the duct through a slot in its bottom wall 14 cm right of the midline and 29 cm in front of the bases, drops to the table, runs back toward the robot and left to about 3 cm right of the midline and 8 to 12 cm in front of the bases, rises, and turns right onto the stand. Stand: a dark-grey plastic stand (two posts 2 x 16 mm with low side lips) centred 17 cm in front of the bases and 13 cm right of the midline. The wire's last 8 cm lies on it with the ferrule pointing forward and sloping 15 degrees down like the entry, the collar's front face 9.25 cm above the table.
scoring: Score 0 if, at any time, the ferrule's tip goes more than 1 mm into any terminal entry other than X1:4's upper entry. Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 if the wire's end is raised 1 cm or more above its place on the stand; 0.5 if the ferrule's tip is also inside X1:4's upper entry, 1 mm or more past the mouth; 0.75 if it is also pushed home: the collar within 0.8 mm of the entry's mouth and the clamp engaged on the ferrule (the clamping spring's leg deflected by the ferrule, checked by the tug below holding at least partly, or with a 2.5 mm screwdriver test in the operating slot); 1.0 if the after-release check also passes. Dropping the wire is not penalised by itself. After-release check, once both grippers have been at least 6 cm from the wire end for 1 s (or at the end of the run): mark the insulation with a pen at the entry's mouth, then pull the wire end straight back out along the entry's axis with a spring scale, raising the pull to 50 N over 0.5 s and holding it for 1.5 s. It passes if the mark moves out less than 1.5 mm. If it fails, the score is 0.75 (or 0.5 if the collar was never home). Distances are read with a rule, or from a close-up photo with a scale in view.
reset_notes: Push a 2.5 mm flat screwdriver into X1:4's operating slot to open the clamp, and pull the wire out. Lay the end back on the stand with the ferrule forward, and the cable along its starting path from the duct slot (the path in the setup photo). About 1 minute.
fidelity: PhysX at 480 Hz, arms with the station's i2rt gains. Published: block, entry angle, ferrule and DIN rail sizes. The clamp is a sprung hinged leaf (stand-in for CAGE CLAMP) tuned to hold 50 N; entry channel sized from photos; square colliders. Wire is 16 jointed capsules, stiffness, mass, friction guessed. Landed wires are visual only; target told apart by its blue housing; pad friction raised for the weak gripper; 50 N pull applied in sim after recording. Details in README.
